title: Review of c03's shell-needed-for-metabolism finding: replicates on fresh seed 5 (full 25 -> 55 bodies; beta=0 and chi_q=0 both 25 -> 0 by t~490); Supported
summary: I re-ran fch-metabolic world.py, world_beta0.py and world_chiq0.py (from 20261025T0922-c03-fch-metabolic) with labkit on new seed 5 at the finding's settings (100 frames x 400 steps, T=800; rerun/). Bodies at frames 25/43/52/61/100: full 25/39/39/46/55 (25 persistent splits, generation 3, 0 merges); beta=0 25/13/5/0/0; chi_q=0 25/13/5/0/0 (counts.txt). In the beta=0 sheet the catalyst leaks out of the micelles as halos by t~32-104, the bodies fade and the last one is gone by t~488.

observations.E: counts.txt: with the shell's gate (beta=0) or its adsorption (chi_q=0) removed, 25 -> 0 bodies by frame 61 (t~490), against 25 -> 55 in the full world on the same seed
observations.B: rerun/world_beta0/sheet.png t=32-104: catalyst halos outside the bodies once the gate is off; the shell layer is what keeps the catalyst in

controls_run.E: rerun/world_beta0 and rerun/world_chiq0 (matched ablations, same seed)

verdicts.limitation: The two ablations give identical body counts at every sampled frame, here and in the author's numbers, so they probably act through the same single route (no effective gate) and are not independent tests. One fresh seed. The full world's own metabolism is partly by construction (amphiphile made only by the catalyst, with degradation); this finding shows that the boundary layer is necessary, which is what it claims.
